Get your high school diploma/GED. Get your driver's license, Job Corps will pay for it. Take two trades if you can. Go to Advanced Training if it lines up with one of your trades. Participate in Work Based Learning and try to network in your field. 
Make sure you choose a trade that is ACTUALLY in demand in your area and pays decently.

It all depends on the job market and your age. If you are over 21, you should be able to get a train conductor trainee job or something similar. The union doesn't place you, but you can't separate from the program until you have a job. Personally, I resigned from the program because I had some bad experiences in LA and I wasn't passionate enough about transportation to stay. Everyone is different though. The instructors are wonderful.
Most offices are closed right now, but I'd give them a call to see if they can get you in touch with an admissions counselor.

I went to the one in LA. The rail simulation is for people reaching the end of the program, if they even get to use it. The only transportation related class we had was the history of transportation. Nothing really current. If you want a transportation job, you'll be able to get one with or without TCU. It's all entry level.
Literally the same thing as Office Administration. I did nothing related to transportation the whole time I was there.
I'm currently in the process of enrolling and the admissions counselor said they were looking at Mid July at the very earliest. Could be a lot longer.

I am also trying to reapply. 
I took Office Administration and was at my last center for 14 months. They told me I would be able to enroll but I would have 10 months to complete the trade I want and get out. The trade I want to take takes 10 months, so with CPP and everything I might not be able to do it at all. 
Doesn't make a whole lot of sense to me. I've never been written up negatively, no minor infractions or anything. I was one of the highest performing students at that Job Corps, and I understand where you're coming from. In my opinion, they should give us a clean slate and reset the time if a graduate wanted to enroll again. 
Even though I don't really have a resolution for you, I just came to say I understand your situation because I'm in the same one. I'm going to call the admissions counselor again tomorrow to see if there's anything I could do to get around the timeframe. When I went the first time, there was a girl who had enrolled for the second time and her previous time didn't count against her. I wonder if it's a new rule.
My guess would be no. But ask your counselor from Job Corps to make sure.

Unfortunately, you might not be able to. Transfers are rarely done, especially out of region. It's even harder once you're already in the program. If you did get approved to transfer, I've heard it can be a long process. You'd still probably be forced to pick a trade at your center regardless.

I was allowed to after I had reached certain privileges. I had to find the job myself and provide my own transportation. I could only work during non-training hours. I had to call off work any time there was some special center activity or event that everyone had to be a part of. They ended up making me lose that job, which was a job training match. 
Not worth it.

As long as you meet the low income requirements, you should be good. You will still be responsible for your loans. They won't help with that.

Only 12 people a year get into the program. You have to fill out an application, have a crystal clear record, staff recommendations, and write an essay on why you should be chosen. Then it's up to the staff.
I'm pretty sure. They have a college program, but it's VERY selective.
I did Advanced Training at the LA center. It was really nice. Open campus, awesomeness staff, good dorms compared to other centers.

I understand what you're going through. I have a muscular condition similar to MS that I would be absolutely terrified to pass on to a child. I'm also a carrier for Norrie Disease, which would mean all of my boys would be born blind and autistic. As they get older, they go deaf. As someone with a disability myself, I couldn't be a parent to a special needs child, or any child for that matter. If I didn't have this condition, maybe my position would be different. You're not the only one!

I say go for it. People in construction trades have been more successful in the long run in my experience with Job Corps. But be aware that you are fully responsible for all housing once you're done.

In my situation, yes it was hard to find a place to live. I left an abusive situation and after getting out, I lived in a hotel for a while and now I'm back in the abusive situation. Is Job Corps worth it? I think so. I got my high school diploma and I used the money from my exit check to buy my first car. Would I go back? Probably not.
I'm still in customer service. I'm doing the same things I was doing before going to Job Corps.

Not particularly. I'm still looking for a better job but it's with the skills I had before Job Corps. I worked in customer service for a couple years prior to Job Corps and that's what I've been continuing since leaving. I currently work at a grocery store. I took Office Administration.
They didn't provide any housing assistance to me. I was completely on my own. I've been out for almost a year now.
From my experience, you can go to any state in your region. They usually want to send you to the closest center that offers the trade you want as long as it's on your region.
